'''''Alpinia zerumbet''''', commonly known as '''shell ginger''' among [[#Names|other names]],  is a [[perennial plant|perennial]] [[species]] of [[Zingiberaceae|ginger]] native to [[East Asia]]. The plants can grow up to {{convert|8|to|10|ft|m|order=flip||round=0.5|sp=us}} tall and bear colorful funnel-shaped flowers. They are grown as ornamentals and their leaves are used in cuisine and traditional medicine.

==Names==
''Alpinia zerumbet'' is called a "shell ginger" or "shell flower" most commonly, because its individual pink flowers, especially when in bud, resemble sea shells. Other common names in [[English language|English]] include "pink porcelain lily", "variegated ginger, and "light galangal".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Datiles |first=Marianne Jennifer |date=2014-03-06 |title=Alpinia zerumbet (shell ginger) |url=https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/full/10.1079/cabicompendium.109799 |journal=CABI Compendium |volume=CABI Compendium |article-number=109799 |doi=10.1079/cabicompendium.109799|url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In Japan, ''A. zerumbet'' is called ''gettō'' ({{lang|ja|ゲットウ [月桃]}}) in standard [[Japanese language|Japanese]].  In the languages of the [[Ryukyu Islands]], it is known as ''sannin'' ({{lang|ja|サンニン}}) [[Okinawan language|on Okinawa]], ''shanin'' ({{lang|ja|シャニン}}) on [[Tanegashima]] in the Ōsumi Islands, ''sa'nen'' ({{lang|ja|サネン}}) [[Amami Ōshima language|on Amami Ōshima]], ''sani'' ({{lang|ja|サニ}}) [[Okinoerabu language|on Okinoerabujima]], ''samin'' ({{lang|ja|サミン}}) [[Miyakoan language|on Miyako-jima]], ''samin'' ({{lang|ja|サミン}}), ''sa'nin'' ({{lang|ja|サニン}}) and ''sami'' ({{lang|ja|サミ}}) [[Ishigaki dialect|on Ishigaki Island]], ''sami'' ({{lang|ja|サミ}}) [[Taketomi dialect|on Taketomi Island]] and ''sa'nin'' ({{lang|ja|サニン}}) [[Iriomote dialect|on Iriomote Island]].  It is known as ''souka'' ({{lang|ja|ソウカ}}) on [[Chichijima]] in the Bonin Islands and ''sōka'' ({{lang|ja|ソーカ}}) in the [[Daitō Islands]] east of the Ryukyus.<ref>[https://note.com/aroma_mokutsuyu/n/nd409df92a93b "月桃の香りや効果効能がパワフル！"] Retrieved 5 July 2023. {{inlang|ja}}</ref><ref>[http://www.gettou.info/name-gettou.html "由来記月桃" [The origin of 'getto'<nowiki>]</nowiki>] at 月桃インフォメーション [Alpinia zerumbet information]. Retrieved 5 July 2023. {{inlang|ja}}</ref>

In Taiwan, ''A. zerumbet'' is called ''yuètáo'' ({{lang|zh|月桃}}) in [[Mandarin Chinese]], ''hó͘-chú-hoe'' ({{lang|zh|虎子花}}) or ''ge̍h-thô''/''go̍eh-thô'' ({{lang|zh|月桃}}) in [[Taiwanese Hokkien]] ''kiéu-kiông'' ({{lang|zh|枸薑}}) or ''ngie̍t-thò'' ({{lang|zh|月桃}}) in [[Siyen Hakka]].  In the island's aboriginal languages, it is known as ''silu'' in [[Bunun language|Bunun]], ''jiaboe'' and ''garyo'' in [[Paiwan language|Paiwan]], ''bussiyan'', ''bissiyan'' and ''bassiyan'' in [[Atayal language|Atayal]]<ref>[https://tai2.ntu.edu.tw/species/639%20001%2020%200 "Alpinia zerumbet (Pers.) B. L. Burtt & R. M. Smith"] at Plants of Taiwan. ([https://web.archive.org/web/20160304202833/http://tai2.ntu.edu.tw/PlantInfo/species-name.php?code=639%20001%2020%200 Archived]) Retrieved 5 July 2023. {{inlang|en|zh}}</ref> and ''lalengac'' in [[Sakizaya language|Sakizaya]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSmmIBWbjFw Kapah kanen kapah malakazali ku lalengac 2018-06-16 Sakizaya IPCF-TITV 原文會 原視族語新聞] Retrieved 5 July 2023. {{inlang|szy}}</ref>

In China, it is called ''yànshānjiāng'' ({{lang|zh|艷山薑}}), as well as ''yùtáo'' ({{lang|zh|玉桃}}), ''cǎoběn zhíwù'' ({{lang|zh|草本植物}}) and ''dà húluóbo'' ({{lang|zh|大胡蘿蔔}}) among other names.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia| encyclopedia=香港浸會大學中醫藥學院藥用植物圖像數據庫| title=艷山薑 Yanshanjiang  | volume=| pages=| url=http://libproject.hkbu.edu.hk/was40/detail?record=1&channelid=1288&searchword=%28Alpinia+zerumbet%29&extension=all&sortfield=%2Bname_formal_latin_sort| access-date=2011-09-02| archive-date=2017-03-05| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305001623/http://libproject.hkbu.edu.hk/was40/detail?record=1&channelid=1288&searchword=%28Alpinia+zerumbet%29&extension=all&sortfield=%2Bname_formal_latin_sort}} {{inlang|zh}}</ref>

== Characteristics ==
Native to eastern Asia, ''Alpinia zerumbet'' is a rhizomatous, evergreen tropical perennial that grows in upright clumps {{convert|8|to|10|ft|m|abbr=on}} tall in tropical climates.  It bears funnel-formed flowers. Flowers have white or pink [[Petal|perianths]] with yellow [[Labellum (botany)|labella]] with red spots and stripes.<ref name=DiscoverNature>
{{Cite web | url= https://www.jcu.edu.au/discover-nature-at-jcu/plants/plants-by-scientific-name2/alpinia-zerumbet | last1= Jackes | first1= Betsy | date= 14 Dec 2012 | title= ''Alpinia zerumbet'' (Shell Ginger, Pink Porcelain Lily) | work= Discover Nature at JCU. Plants on Cairns Campus | location= Australia | publisher= James Cook University | access-date= 17 May 2013 }}
</ref> There are three [[stamen]]s, but only one has [[pollen]]. There is one [[pistil]]. The fruit is globose with many striations. In more typical conditions, it reaches {{convert|4|to|8|ft|m|abbr=on}} feet tall in the green house, and {{convert|3|to|4|ft|m|abbr=on}} feet tall, as a house plant.<ref name="eol">{{cite web
|url=http://www.eol.org/pages/1126734
|title=''Alpinia zerumbet'' (Pers.) B. L. Burtt & R. M. Sm.
|publisher=Encyclopedia of Life
|access-date= March 19, 2011
}}</ref>

It was originally called ''Alpinia speciosa'', which was also the scientific name of [[Etlingera elatior|torch ginger]]. To avoid the confusion, it was renamed ''A. zerumbet'' while torch ginger was reclassified in the genus ''Etlingera''. No species is accepted as ''A. speciosa'' today.<ref>{{ThePlantList| id=kew-219058| taxon=Alpinia speciosa| authority = (J.C.Wendl.) K.Schum. | accessdate = 2023-07-05}} </ref>

[[File:Alpinia zerumbet2.jpg|thumb|right|''Alpinia zerumbet'']]

==Cultivation==
''Alpinia zerumbet'' is best grown in rich medium-wet, to wet well drained soils in full sun to part shade. Afternoon shade in hot summer climates, is recommended. Indoors, the plant must have bright light and humid conditions. Flowering rarely occurs before the second year.{{cn|date=June 2025}}

==Uses==
The long leaf blades of ''A. zerumbet'' are used for wrapping ''[[zongzi]]'', a traditional Chinese dish made of rice stuffed with different fillings. In Okinawa, Japan, its leaves are sold for making an herbal tea and are also used to flavor noodles and wrap ''[[muchi]]'' rice cakes.{{cn|date=June 2025}}

A 2013 publication found ''A. zerumbet'' leaf extract increased the lifespan of ''C. elegans'' by 22.6%.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bouthier |first1=Antoine |title=Okinawan plant holds promise of elixir of youth |url=https://www.bworldonline.com/content.php?section=Opinion&title=Okinawan-plant-holds-promise-of-elixir-of-youth&id=81204 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226213002/https://www.bworldonline.com/content.php?section=Opinion&title=Okinawan-plant-holds-promise-of-elixir-of-youth&id=81204 |archive-date=2021-02-26 |access-date=4 November 2018 |website=Business World Online |publisher=BusinessWorld Publishing}}</ref>  Recent research has investigated its effects on human [[longevity]] and the [[phytochemicals]] that may be responsible.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Teschke |first1=Rolf |last2=Xuan |first2=Tran Dang |title=Viewpoint: A Contributory Role of Shell Ginger (Alpinia zerumbet) for Human Longevity in Okinawa, Japan? |journal=Nutrients |volume=10 |issue=2 |page=166 |publisher=US National Institute of Health |pmc=5852742 |year=2018 |pmid=29385084 |doi=10.3390/nu10020166 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

''A. zerumbet'' contains many [[kavalactones]] structurally related to the compounds in [[kava]] (''Piper methysticum'') and may{{clarify|date=July 2023}} help prevent high glucose induced cell damage in human umbilical vein endothelial cells.<ref>{{Cite journal | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/14786419.2021.2023866?journalCode=gnpl20 | doi=10.1080/14786419.2021.2023866 | title=Kavalactones isolated from Alpinia zerumbet (Pers.)
